correctness.rationale: Every point image is fixed, and every nonempty block maps wholly to one block. For each idempotent induced block map, choose r fixed points in a root of capacity s and send its M−r remaining fiber points independently to them, giving H_s(M) and the product over roots. A separate exact replay confirmed 21 rooted counts, all 31 ordered positive block-size profiles with total size at most five, and 30 endpoint-inclusive binomial increments. For M/n→t and s/n→1, the consecutive-term ratio decreases because both its positive rational prefactor and its nonnegative power factor decrease. At r∼cn/log n its log is (t/c−1)log n+o(log n). Using test points halfway from t to each fixed tail threshold, the ratio over Θ(n/log n) intervening indices is bounded by n raised to a strictly signed constant. Each tail therefore has normalized mass exp(−Ω(n)) after allowing O(n) terms. The maximum lies at r∼tn/log n; at such r, log binom(s,r)=o(n), r log r=tn+o(n), and the leading coefficient of log(n/log n) must be the actual M, not tn. This gives the root-weight expansion. The common N log(n/log n) term cancels for all induced maps; among at least two fibers the largest sum of t_a log t_a is realized by (m−1,1), giving the stated exponent even for near-equal sizes. For capacity u=n+o(n), the added r=u+1 summand divided by H_u(N) has log −(1+o(1))n log n. On the saddle window the multiplier (u+1)/(u+1−R) is 1+R/(u+1)+O(1/log² n); the uniform exponential tail absorbs the O(u) maximum. Arbitrarily small fixed windows give the uniform increment (m+o(1))/log n. Signed telescoping at fixed N proves the odds formula, including ties, floors and both sublogarithmic and superlogarithmic gap conclusions. The proof does not cover growing m or non-equal limiting block proportions; no finite test is used to infer a limit.

value.rationale: The symmetric idempotent model has an intrinsic question about how much capacity asymmetry changes which block receives all images. The theorem gives a quantitative sharp crossover: smaller gaps wash out, arbitrary finite log-odds arise at logarithmic gaps, and a uniquely larger gap selects a winner. That information is invisible in the leading entropy rate and is scientifically useful beyond the finite enumeration.
